explain.say: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day? You probably know that line. It opens Sonnet 18, one of 154 sonnets by Shakespeare printed in 1609. A sonnet is fourteen lines with a strict shape, and the chain shows how Shakespeare builds one.

explain.say: First the rhythm. Each line has ten syllables in five beats: da-DUM, da-DUM. Look at the word compare: com-PARE, an iamb, soft then strong. Five of those make iambic pentameter. Tap the beat: shall I com-PARE thee TO a SUM-mer's DAY. Can you hear it?

draw.note: An iamb: soft then strong, com-PARE

explain.say: Now the shape. Three quatrains, four lines each, then a couplet. The first two quatrains say summer is too short and the sun dims. Then the turn, the volta: but thy eternal summer shall not fade. The couplet clinches it: so long lives this, and this gives life to thee. What is this?

explain.say: The sonnets tell a story. Look at the sort: sonnets 1 to 126 mostly address a beautiful young man, the Fair Youth. Sonnets 127 to 152 address a Dark Lady. Sonnet 130 begins: my mistress' eyes are nothing like the sun, mocking the usual flattery. Why might honesty be more loving?

Shakespeare reshaped an Italian form. On the left, Petrarch's octave and sestet. On the right, Shakespeare's three quatrains and a couplet. Lovely work. Exam tip: always find the volta and say what changes there. Challenge: write a rhyming couplet that turns an argument round.

faq.q: What is the volta in a sonnet?
faq.a: The turn, where the argument or mood shifts. In a Petrarchan sonnet it comes at line nine; in a Shakespearean sonnet it may come at line nine or at the closing couplet.
A line of ten syllables in five iambs, each a soft beat followed by a strong one: da-DUM, five times. It is the main metre of Shakespeare's verse.
The young man addressed in sonnets 1 to 126, urged at first to marry and have children, then praised and immortalised. His real identity is unknown; the Earl of Southampton is one guess.
asks: Who are the sonnets written to?

faq.a: The woman addressed in sonnets 127 to 152, described as dark-haired and dark-eyed, with whom the speaker has a jealous, troubled affair. Her identity is unknown.

faq.q: How is a Shakespearean sonnet different from a Petrarchan sonnet?
faq.a: A Petrarchan sonnet has an eight-line octave and six-line sestet, rhymed abbaabba then cdecde or similar. A Shakespearean sonnet has three quatrains and a couplet, rhymed abab cdcd efef gg.

facts: Shakespeare's 154 sonnets were published in 1609 by Thomas Thorpe.
The 1609 edition is dedicated to a mysterious Mr. W. H.
Sonnet 130 parodies the Petrarchan habit of comparing a lover to the sun, coral and roses.
